transcript_body:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 14:00 UTC - 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Rajesh Kumar (Cumulus Head of Partnerships), Emily Park (Cumulus Cloud Solutions), Dmitri Ivanov (Cumulus Infrastructure Lead)

[00:00] Liam: hey everybody, thanks for joining, i'm liam carter from redwood, i'm the ae on this. quick intro, priya's our se and she'll do the technical bits, um, how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Rajesh: good, good, thanks liam - excited to chat, quick note we're in sfo region mostly but we do have some eu capacity, emily will cover that
[00:20] Emily: yep, mostly sfo/us-west and ams for europe, small apac footprint in sg
[00:27] Priya: great, i'll give a quick runbook on how we usually partner with gpu/cloud vendors and then we can go into integration options - api-based reseller, dedicated pools or private deployments (vpc/on-prem), sound good?
[00:38] Rajesh: perfect, we want to understand commercials and technical lift, also how we can co-sell and what the pilot looks like

[01:05] Priya: from a technical lens, redwood provides three main modes: hosted api for fast time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private (vpc/on-prem) for regulated customers. partners we work with fall into two patterns: 1) resell hosted/dedicated and let us manage runtime; 2) deep integration where partner provides the gpu infra and we ship a private control plane.
[01:30] Dmitri: quick q, for private control plane, do you require any special network topology or specific k8s version? we run k8s 1.26 on-prem with calico, and nvlink-enabled a100/h100 nodes
[01:45] Priya: good question. our private package supports k8s 1.24+ typically, calico is fine, we do need worker nodes with gpu drivers and access to nvidia container toolkit; nvlink is supported at infra level but not strictly required. there are a few kernel modules we recommend, we'll share the infra checklist. note: transcripts sometimes mangle nvidia/nvlink so docs are clearer than speech.
[02:10] Liam: on commercials - partners can either resell hosted/dedicated with revenue share, or we do a consumption pass-through model for private deployments; margins depend on committed capacity and support SLAs. we'll share a partner one-pager after this.

[03:00] Rajesh: regarding latency and cost, customers ask about batching vs single-token latency - how do you help partners pick quantization and performance profiles?
[03:18] Priya: we have redwood optimize recommendations - it looks at sequence distribution and suggests batching and quantization profiles, also kv/prefix cache for steady-state workloads. for partner pilots we run a benchmark suite: simple prompts + p95/p99 latency targets and cost per 1k tokens. we'll share a mock spreadsheet.
[03:45] Emily: can you share that benchmark sheet now?
[03:48] Liam: i'll drop the link in the notes - https://share.redwood/mock-benchmarks.xlsx (placeholder)

[04:20] Dmitri: security - we need details on encryption, kms, sso/saml, and audit logs. any gotchas for fips/hsm?
[04:32] Priya: redwood supports customer-managed kms/hsm integrations in private mode; hosted has envelope encryption and at-rest encryption, and we've completed soc2 type 2. for fips specifics we can loop in security and share the security pack.
[04:48] Rajesh: ok that matters for a bunch of our finance customers

[05:10] [short crosstalk - connection dips briefly]

[05:40] Priya: about routing and fallbacks - you can configure policies to route by latency/cost/region and fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained; partners use that to maintain uptime during spikes
[06:01] Dmitri: does the runtime select kernels automatically for h100 vs a100?
[06:07] Priya: yes, compilation and kernel selection is part of the runtime - it picks optimized kernels and quantization-friendly paths based on model and hardware characteristics, though manual tuning can help for custom infra

[06:40] Rajesh: what about support and SLAs for dedicated pools? our enterprise customers expect 99.9 uptime and burst capacity
[06:53] Liam: dedicated comes with configurable autoscaling and SLA options - 99.9 is in the typical offering with premium support; pricing varies by reserved commit. we can draft a sample SOW

[07:20] Emily: interested in co-sell motion - do you have channel programs?
[07:28] Liam: yes, we have a partner program with co-marketing credits, joint case studies, and lead routing; we'll include program docs in follow-up

[08:00] Priya: quick note on observability - the console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks, which partners use to justify tco to customers

[09:05] Rajesh: ok helpful, let's talk pilot - typical pilot length and success criteria?
[09:15] Priya: pilots are usually 4-6 weeks: validate perf (p95/p99), cost per token, and integration stability (auth, routing, metrics). success = meeting agreed latency and cost targets and a decision to proceed to commercial roll-out

[10:00] Dmitri: for technical deep dive we'll need sample models: Llama-2 variants and a few open HF models, and tests with fp16/4-bit quantized weights, can you support that?
[10:12] Priya: yes, we support common open models and quantized weights; we'll propose a test matrix

[11:00] Rajesh: do you integrate with partner billing or should we reconcile separately?
[11:10] Liam: two options: partners resell and handle billing, or redwood invoices customers directly and we allocate revenue share. both supported depending on legal preference

[12:00] Emily: marketplace integrations - can we list jointly?
[12:08] Liam: we support cloud marketplace listings and joint marketplace offers for dedicated/private; will add marketplace checklist to follow-up

[13:30] Priya: infra checklist items we'll share: k8s version, gpu type (a100/h100), driver versions, network egress rules (control plane access), kms endpoints, and ntp/time sync
[14:05] Dmitri: regarding network egress, does private control plane need persistent outbound to redwood endpoints? we prefer minimal egress for air-gapped customers
[14:16] Priya: for fully air-gapped we offer an on-prem package; for vpc-private we need control plane endpoints reachable for management, but you can opt for a local-only runtime with a mediated handshake. details in the tech deep dive

[18:00] Rajesh: competitors - customers mention Lambda and Paperspace - how does redwood compare on throughput and pricing?
[18:12] Liam: we emphasize production-first experience and cost-aware controls; performance depends on model/hw but runtime optimizations and caching often reduce per-token costs versus naive hosting. we'll include benchmark comparisons where possible

[22:00] Emily: legal/procurement - we'll need an nda and partner terms, any partner agreement template?
[22:10] Liam: yes, we'll push an NDA and partner agreement template; legal prefers mutual nda then partner mspa/doc

[28:00] Priya: recap action items: liam send partner one-pager + pricing matrix, priya share infra checklist + security pack and schedule tech deep dive, rajesh share fleet inventory and preferred pilot regions
[28:25] Rajesh: will do
[28:30] Liam: i'll follow up by email with the links and target dates

[30:00] Meeting end - thanks and sign off

Notes/Links shared in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/partner-playbook, https://share.redwood/mock-benchmarks.xlsx (benchmark template), https://redwood.ai/security/security-pack.pdf (security pack placeholder)

End transcript.
